ns2:course.label: Energy Economics
ns2:course.description: Use of economics tools to understand and evaluate public policy issues surrounding energy markets and related environmental markets. Focus is on the economic drivers of energy production and use, biofuel policy, transportation and storage of energy commodities, regulation of energy markets, and policies designed to mitigate the impact of energy production and consumption on the environment. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. Prerequisite: ECON 302 or equivalent.
